safety_lead_time.comparison_action: REDUCE — recommended 2.66 days vs SAP 3.00 days

narrative: Demand for PL2__M697940D is lumpy (CV=0.90) with 94.8% active working days and no detectable trend over the 96-day history. Lead times are very short (mean 0.24 days) and stable. The EOQ of 7,292 units far exceeds the MOQ of 946 units, enabling infrequent large replenishments (~8.4 orders/year) that slash ordering cost by 94%. A z-scaled safety stock of 155 units at 95% service level is sufficient given the short, stable lead time, replacing the overstated SAP safety stock of 788 units.
warnings: Storage utilisation at 96.8% (7,447 / 7,693 units) — any safety stock increase must be reviewed against capacity ceiling.
8 demand outliers detected and winsorised at upper bound 497.69 units.

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) continuous-review reorder-point with EOQ lot size
research_insights.selection_rationale: With near-daily active demand (94.8%), a stable sub-day lead time, and a high CV requiring explicit safety stock sizing, the continuous-review (r,Q) policy is the appropriate choice. It minimises total cost via EOQ while the reorder point absorbs lead-time demand uncertainty.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The recommended policy (SS=155, OQ=7292) utilises 96.8% of the 7,692-unit storage capacity. Any future increase in safety stock (e.g., due to service level uplift or lead time deterioration) risks breaching the capacity ceiling and would require either a capacity expansion or a reduction in OQ below EOQ optimum.
